title: Story behind 300-year-old Scots hotel branded 'one of the most haunted'
excerpt: Visitors have reported plenty of spooky sights while staying there
content:
Spooky stories behind 300-year-old Scots hotel branded 'one of the most haunted in Britain'

Visitors have reported plenty of spooky sights while staying there

13:08, 29 Sep 2026

With Halloween around the corner, many people are getting into the spooky spirit by attending themed events or watching their favourite horror films. However, for those wanting to fully immerse themselves in the Halloween spirit, they may want to try staying at a Scottish hotel that is allegedly filled with ghosts.

‌

Located at the northern tip of Loch Lomond in the hamlet of Inverarnan is the Drovers Inn. First opened back in 1705, the property is rumoured to be one of the most haunted hotels in Britain.

‌

With more than 300 years of history, some guests have reported spooky happenings while staying at the Scottish hotel. From strange lights to photos being taken as the guests sleep, the Drovers Inn has become well known for its ghostly sightings.

‌

Sharing some of the scary tales, one of the most notable paranormal sightings dates all the way back to 1792. Otherwise known as the Year of the Sheep, a young crofting family at the time was removed from where they lived so landlords could make profit from sheep farming.

With little means to support their young child, the family were said to travel south in hopes of starting a new life. However, after being caught in a heavy snowstorm, the family sadly froze to death while trying to find shelter at the Drovers Inn.

‌

Over the years there have been accounts of people seeing a young family wandering the land during the winter months. However, one of the spookiest accounts recall a couple waking up to a cold shiver and finding the family standing at the end of the bed as the young boy gave a cheery wave.

Along with a bar and restaurant, the Drovers Inn has 15 uniquely styled rooms that feature oil paintings, rich colours and antique furniture. However, it is room six that is noted to be the 'haunted room'.

A couple recently stayed in room six for a night in October. During their stay, the girlfriend allegedly woke up to seeing flickering lights in the room. After dismissing it as the fire alarm light, the boyfriend opened his eyes to see up to 20 white points of light dancing around in mid air.

‌

With the room said to be pitch black at the time, the couple tried to rationalise it as fireflies. However, this was dismissed by staff who said they weren't likely to inhabit the area.

Other guests have also reported incidents after taking photographs at the inn. One woman was at the hotel for a birthday treat with her daughter and friends.

A few days after her stay, she emailed the manager wondering if they could tell them who the little girl in the pink dress was that featured in their photo taken on the hotel's stairs. Her confusion peaked as she didn't recall seeing the child - or any other children - at the hotel that night.

‌

On top of this, her daughter, who took the photo, was adamant that the little girl was not there when she took the photo on her phone. While the party wanted to get answers, they were met with none.

The inn responded that there were no children staying at the hotel that evening. It also added that there were no children visiting at the time. The mystery of the little girl has since remained just that, a mystery.

Other guests have also reported seeing and hearing a ghost wandering the halls screaming in pain, while others have woken up in their rooms feeling a "small icy cold and wet body" next to them in bed.
